notes: On 6 January 2022, dozens of protesters held a 'pro-democracy' demonstration in Oreland (Pennsylvania) as part of nationwide events commemorating the anniversary of the 6 January 2021 Capitol riots.

On 13 January 2022, about a dozen nurses rallied outside Research Medical Center in Kansas City (Missouri) to call for more staff and for more coronavirus health measures in the workplace. The protest was organized by National Nurses United as a part of a country-wide rally.

On 15 January 2022, a small number of people gathered at Court Square in Harrisonburg (Virginia) to stand in solidarity with Amazon workers attempting to unionize in Bessemer, Alabama and to call on Amazon to stop interfering in these efforts. The rally was hosted by Community Solidarity with the Poultry Workers.

On 16 January 2022, dozens of people gathered outside the Islamic Cultural Center in New York - Bronx (New York) to urge New York City leaders to investigate the owners of the Twin Parks North West apartment and to mourn the 15 people who died in the Twin Parks fire.

On 19 January 2022, supporters of an indigenous demonstrator rallied outside of the federal courthouse in Tucson (Arizona) after she was acquitted of charges stemming from a protest against the border wall in September 2020, where she refused to vacate a construction site near Quitobaquito Springs, a sacred O'odham site. The demonstrator, a Hia C-ed O'odham and Tohono O'odham woman, addressed the crowd as she left the courthouse.

On 16 January 2022, about 20 unhoused people and volunteers from the Boise Mutual Aid Collective set up tents and gathered for a protest at the corner of North Sixth and West Jefferson streets in downtown Boise (Idaho) against the treatment of homeless people and to demand more housing.

On 6 January 2022, demonstrators staged a 'Day of Remembrance and Action' rally and 'Defend our Democracy' vigil at Peace Corner in Memorial Park in downtown DeKalb (Illinois) in support of voting rights legislation. The DeKalb County League of Women Voters and REACT (Responsive Engagement Activating Civic Talent) organized the event to commemorate the 1-year anniversary of the Capitol riots.

On 15 January 2022, demonstrators that consisted of local renters and others affiliated with the Neighborhood Assistance Corporation of America gathered outside of the home of Department of Community Affairs commissioner Christopher Nunn in Atlanta (Georgia) to protest against the slow deployment of the federal emergency rental assistance program that was enacted due to the coronavirus pandemic.

On 10 January 2022, sanitation workers unionized with the Teamsters Local 542 protested in San Diego (California) in their 4th week of a labor strike against employer Republic Services. The workers demanded fair contracts, working hours, and improvements to workplace safety.

On 15 January 2022, around 30 to 40 people gathered at downtown in Bowling Green (Kentucky) to support voting rights. The event was hosted by the Kentucky League of Women Voters. Members of NAACP attended.

On 24 January 2023, hundreds of American Airlines flight attendants picketed at Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (Texas) to protest for pay raises. This demonstration was part of a nation-wide demonstration organized by the Association of Flight Attendants at around a dozen airports.

On 8 January 2023, an unreported number of people rallied outside the Museum of Art in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to demonstrate against the death of Mahsa Amini in Iran as well as to honor those who died in the downing of Ukrainian Flight PS752 in Iran. Members of the Iranian community and Philly Iran participated in the demonstration which took place as part of a worldwide series of protests against the Iranian regime on the third anniversary of the downing of PS752 organized by The Association of Families of Flight PS752 Victims.

On 18 January 2023, demonstrators gathered in New Iberia (Louisiana) to memorialize a 14-year old Black teenager who was found dead on 16 January 2023. Demonstrators called for justice and an end to violence. Family members were also present.

On 17 January 2023, protesters and members of New Jersey League of Conservation Voters, New Jersey's Sierra Club chapter, and the New Jersey Organizing Project gathered in Atlantic City (New Jersey) to refute the claim that the offshore wind projects caused the deaths of seven whales since the start of December and to support the project. Protesters said the claims are 'non-scientific, baseless and dangerous.'

On 24 January 2023, dozens of demonstrators, including drag queens, gathered at Missouri's Capitol in Jefferson City (Missouri) to protest against proposed legislation which they say discriminates against LGBT+ individuals. The proposed legislation includes banning trans women from playing female sports and limiting where a drag show can take place.

On 3 January 2023, around 400 protesters including staff and health workers gathered outside Howard Brown Health clinics in several locations across Chicago (Illinois) to protest the recent layoffs of 60+ employees during contract negotiations. The Illinois Nurses Association helped organize these demonstrations.

On 17 January 2023, an unreported number of workers alongside members of the Union of Southern Service Workers demonstrated outside of Dollar General in Irmo (South Carolina) to call for an improvement of working conditions and pay at the company. The protest took place as part of a two-day strike organized by two workers at the store.

On 18 January 2023, over 200 students marched on the Delaware State University campus in Dover (Delaware) to call for the Delaware State University Police Department to improve their response to different kinds of incidents, especially sexual assaults, and to call on University administration to improve safety on campus.

On 16 January 2023, about a dozen students and parents gathered outside the Olentangy Local Schools administrative building in Lewis Center (Ohio) to protest the recent decision of a communications official to stop a third-grade teacher from reading Dr. Seuss' 'The Sneetches' on an NPR podcast when students, prompted by the story, asked questions about race, critical race theory, and racial discrimination.

Around 7 January 2023 (weekend of), demonstrators including students and affiliates of Time Youth Dothan gathered at the Houston County Courthouse in Dothan (Alabama) to call for an end to gun violence. This follows the recent fatal shootings of some youth members of Time Youth Dothan.

On 17 January 2024, about 25 people, including members of Emancipate NC and victim's family members, gathered in Raleigh (North Carolina) to demand justice for an African American man who died after being tasered by police last year and accountability from the police department.

On 18 January 2024, almost 20 people dressed in bridal gowns held a demonstration in the state Capitol in Olympia (Washington) to support efforts to ban child marriages in the state. Unchained At Last, Zonta International and the AHA Foundation were present.

Around 18 January 2024 (as reported), White Lives Matter affiliates gathered in Alabama (coded as Montgomery (Alabama)) to demonstrate in favor of White Lives Matter, hold antisemitic signs, and promote the group.

On 6 January 2024, 30 demonstrators rallied at May Day Plaza in Minneapolis (Minnesota) to demand that the US Supreme Court continue to allow access to the abortion drug mifepristone amid the review of a ruling which could limit the drug's accessibility. Those present included members of the MN Anti-War Committee, MN Abortion Action Committee (MNAAC), Twin Cities Coalition for Justice 4 Jamar, and MN Immigrant Rights Action Committee.

On 12 January 2024, members of the LGBTQ+ community and Fairness West Virginia gathered at the State Capitol in Charleston (West Virginia) to support a bill which would prohibit job, housing, and public accommodation discrimination for LBGTQ+ people.

source: 5 On Your Side; KMOV4; KWMU; St. Louis Post-Dispatch
notes: On 18 January 2024, hundreds of students walked out of class to hold a rally at Francis Howell High School and Francis Howell North High School in Saint Charles (Missouri) to protest against the Francis Howell School Board's decision to remove Black History and Black Literature courses due to the courses' connection to the 'Social Justice Standards: The Teaching Tolerance Anti-Bias Framework.'

On 8 January 2024, about 50 pro-Palestinian demonstrators rallied outside the State Capitol in Phoenix (Arizona) to denounce a pro-Israel resolution that the legislature had just passed and to demand support for Palestinian 'freedom', a permanent ceasefire in Gaza, and an end to U.S. support for Israel's 'genocide' amid the Israel-Hamas war which began in October 2023. The demonstration was organized by the Palestinian American Community Center and joined by the Navajo Nation, O'odham indigenous supporters, JVP, Socialist Revolution, Arizona Palestine Solidarity Alliance, Arizona Muslim Alliance, CAIR, Common Defense, Arizona Palestine Network, and SJP.
On 9 January 2024, workers with UAW Local 1391 rallied in East Dubuque (Illinois) as part of an ongoing labor strike to demand increased pay and an improved contract.

On 11 January 2024, dozens of demonstrators, including Christian faith leaders and educational leaders, gathered outside Chimneyrock Elementary in Memphis (Tennessee) to demonstrate against an After School Satan Club.

On 11 January 2024, protesters rallied in Northampton (Massachusetts) to demand the closure of Guantanamo Bay detention camp due to poor living conditions, as well as what they claimed is 'torture methods and abuse.' No More Guantanamos, Witness Against Torture, CodePink, and Amherst Amnesty International Group 128 organized the rally.
